title: Court Shuttle Relay
description: A team relay of full-court shuttle sprints that trains change of direction, speed and recovery with a competitive edge, finishing a training session with energy.

content.objective: Improve speed and change of direction over short distances while teams compete against each other and against their own best time.
content.setup: Two teams line up at the baseline behind cones. Cones mark the free-throw line, half-court line and far free-throw line on each side of the court.
instructions: The first player sprints to the near free-throw line, touches the floor and sprints back to tag the next player.
The next player runs to the half-court line and back, the third to the far free-throw line and back.
Each player then repeats the sequence in the opposite direction to complete the shuttle.
The first team to have every player complete the shuttle wins the round.
Rest for 60 seconds between rounds and repeat three to four times, recording the times.
coachingPoints: Plant the outside foot and push off hard at every turn.
Stay low on the turn and drive with the arms.
Tag the teammate cleanly before the next player goes.
Encourage teammates and beat your own best time.
commonMistakes: Rounding the turn instead of planting and pushing.
Pacing the first sprint and having nothing left at the end.
content.safety: Run in separate lanes, keep the run-off area clear behind the cones and stop if any player shows signs of fatigue or dizziness.
progressions: Add a second lap or shorten the rest between rounds.
regressions: Reduce the distance to the half-court line or lengthen the rest.
variations: Each player dribbles a ball for the last round.
